newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - July 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - July 8.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- HYDER MAY ISSUE BOND TO COVER 280M STG BILL

Hyder, the Welsh multi-utility, is said to be considering issuing preference shares or a corporate bond to help pay for its windfall tax bill. The company may also announce an end to customer rebates and a tightening of both discretionary spending in the core business and the 30m stg capital expenditure plans it had for its unregulated infrastructure business this year.
-- INCREASE IN SALES BOOSTS WICKES

DIY group Wickes has said it expects to return to the black this year following a restructuring. The forecast follows a statement in May confirming a brisk sales performance for the first quarter. Like-for-like UK sales for Wickes rose by 12 per cent for the first six months to June. Analysts are expecting the group to report full-year pre-tax profits of between 5m stg and 6m stg.
-- SUGAR PRICE FALL SWEET FOR BARR

AG Barr, the Scottish soft drinks manufacturer, has more than trebled its interim pre-tax profits to 3.8m stg. The rise, which came on sales up 8 per cent at 50.1m stg, was helped by a 6 per cent fall in the price of sugar. The company, whose products include Irn Bru and Orangina, is also hoping to benefit to the tune of 1m stg a year from the merging of its three Scottish factories to one in Cumbernauld.
THE TIMES
-- EMU 'WILL CUT PRICES - AND PROFITS'

A report released Tuesday by accountants KPMG claims that monetary union will lead to lower retail prices across Europe and hit corporate profitability. The report forecasts that the single currency will improve price transparency and could drive prices down to the lowest level across the single market. KPMG warns high cost producers that they should be prepared to see their margins cut substantially with a resulting drop in profitability.
-- WEW ISSUES THIRD WARNING

Discount clothing retailer WEW has issued its third profits warning of the year, and revealed that it has asked Coopers & Lybrand Corporate Finance to assess options for the business. WEW said it is considering seeking offers for the business, which, it warned, is likely to make a loss of at least 4m stg for the year to the end of this month. The retailer is also planning to close eight stores by the end of August.
-- BUDGENS TARGETS FORECOURT

Supermarket and convenience store group Budgens has reported a 19.7 per cent increase in pre-tax profit in the year to April 27, to 9.1m stg. Announcing the results, the group said it plans to introduce its petrol station format next year, opening up to 45 outlets on Q8 forecourts. The group is also planning to open a further ten High Street stores this year after opening seven last time, and to refurbish 14 others.
THE GUARDIAN
-- RECORD CITY TAKEOVERS LAND RICH FEES AND BONUSES

According to surveys carried out by Acquisitions Monthly, the Confederation of British Industry and recruitment specialists Robert Walters, London bankers are in line to receive increased bonus payments this year as a result of record levels of corporate takeover and merger activity. Acquisitions Monthly stated fees charged by firms of corporate advisers could rise ten per cent to $1.2bn this year, Robert Walters commented that back office administrators can now earn up to 87,000 stg per year and CBI pointed out while high street banks and insurance companies were forced to make recent job cuts, overall financial sector employment was up.
-- RETAILERS URGED TO THINK ETHICAL

Clare Short, the new Labour government's International Development Secretary, is set to tell companies that boycotting retailers who sell products manufactured in Third World sweatshops is outdated. Short is expected to urge retailers to take advantage of business opportunities in the Third World, while at the same time warning that they cannot afford to ignore increasing consumer interest in the production of goods.
Supermarket chain Sainsbury's, which has completed four pilot schemes in Africa, has welcomed the government's 'new partnership' approach to tackling Third World poverty.
-- MR KIPLING MAKES U-TURN TO RETURN 100M STG SLICE OF CAKE

Manufacturing group Tomkins, the company behind products ranging from Mr Kipling cakes to Smith & Wesson handguns, has changed its mind about a share buyback to return cash to investors. Three months after ruling out the move, Tomkins has announced plans to hand back 100m stg of its 250m stg excess cash within the next three months, and more is likely to follow. Tomkins said part of the decision was based on the inflated prices of takeover targets.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- NATIONAL POWER PENSIONERS GET A SECOND CHANCE

High Court Judge, Mr Justice Robert Walker has given National Power pensioners a second opportunity to fight the company's use of pension scheme surpluses to help fund its post-privatisation redundancy programme. Yesterday's decision could result in National Power having to pay back 100m stg if a court ruled in the pensioners favour. The pensioners are reacting to Ombudsman Julian Farrand's conclusion that the company had "misused" the funds, but National Power continues to deny any "material error".
-- VODAFONE UNVEILS A NEW IMAGE IN CHASE FOR GROWTH

Vodafone, the UK's largest mobile phone group, has launched a new corporate image and announced a rationalisation of its retail branches in an attempt to rejuvenate its flagging subscriber base. The new image will replace the six different High Street brands, which had previously competed against each other, and unite them under one Vodafone logo. Vodafone have said that the new streamlined approach will result in job losses.
-- SEMA SHAKE-UP POINTS TO FRANCE TELECOM SALE

France Telecom has taken a further step toward its expected Fr40bn (4bn stg) autumn partial privatisation after Monday's agreement on a restructuring of its shareholding in Sema, the fast growing IT group. The restructuring leaves France Telecom with a clean 23 per cent interest in Sema and removes a key restriction on Sema expanding into the US IT market. It was welcomed by the market which saw share prices rise 55p to 1342p.
